title: Crystal Quest Water Filter Reviews: Is Crystal Quest Legit, and Is It Worth the Price?
title_tag: Crystal Quest Reviews 2026: Is Crystal Quest Legit?
description: Is Crystal Quest legit? Its shower filter is rated 4.9 out of 5 from 232 reviews and its pitcher 4.8 from 111 on crystalquest.com. Prices, returns and who it suits.
excerpt: Is Crystal Quest legit, and are its water filter pitchers, shower filters and under-sink systems worth buying? Who makes them, what the ratings on its store say, what they cost and the strict return rules.
image_alt: The Crystal Quest water filter pitcher, a clear jug with a white lid and handle and a filter cartridge inside
lede: Crystal Quest makes water filters: pitchers, shower and bath filters, countertop and under-sink systems, reverse osmosis units and whole-house systems. It sells them on its own store at crystalquest.com and is run by Quest Technologies, Inc. in Kennesaw, Georgia. Here's who makes it, what the ratings say, what it costs and what the return rules say.

parts: Crystal Quest is a real US company with a published business address and phone number, and its best sellers are rated 4.8 to 4.9 out of 5 on its own store. The prices are fair for small filters, from $39.95 for a pitcher. The catch is the return policy: you pay return shipping, and a restocking fee of up to 30% can apply, so it suits buyers who know which filter they need.

The range runs from small to very large. At the small end are the Water Pitcher Filter System ($39.95 to $42.95), the Shower Filter ($40.95 to $44.95) and the Bath Ball Filter (from $64.95). In the middle are the SMART countertop filters (from $86.90) and under-sink filters ($149.90 to $208.80), and reverse osmosis under-sink systems from $298.40. At the top are whole-house filters and softeners from about $1,300 to over $10,000.

Many systems come in versions named after what the cartridge targets, such as fluoride, arsenic, lead, nitrate or alkaline. Crystal Quest also sells replacement cartridges, with a subscription, and city and well water tests from $159. Prices checked on November 19, 2026.

parts: The shower filter and the pitcher have the most reviews by far, 232 and 111. The countertop and under-sink systems score just as high but from 12 and 15 reviews, which is too few to lean on. Keep in mind that these ratings are shown by the store itself, and we couldn't check an independent rating on Trustpilot.
The weak point we found is in the rules rather than the ratings: the refund policy itself warns buyers to know their water before ordering, because returns cost shipping and a restocking fee.

Yes, by what we could check. The store lists its business as Quest Technologies, Inc., 175 Chastain Meadows Ct NW, Kennesaw, Georgia, with a toll-free phone number. Its About page says it assembles its products in the USA from US-designed parts and parts from domestic and global suppliers, and that it has an A+ BBB rating; those are the company's own words.

Its product pages state certifications for the filter media; for the pitcher, it says the medium is certified to Standard 42 (aesthetic effects) and by the WQA to Standard 61. The store shows its shipping, refund and contact policies in full.

For the small filters, the prices are in line with other brands: $39.95 for a pitcher, $18 for a pitcher cartridge that Crystal Quest says lasts 2,000 gallons or 6 to 12 months, and $40.95 for a shower filter. The SMART under-sink filter at $149.90 is rated by Crystal Quest for about 10,000 gallons, or 1 to 3 years.

The bigger systems are a bigger decision, and the return rules matter more there: a restocking fee of up to 30% on a $2,000 system is a lot of money. If you aren't sure what your water needs, a water test first is the safer order.
Our [Crystal Quest discount code guide](saving-tips-crystal-quest-discount-code.html) lists every way to pay less, with prices side by side.

parts: Crystal Quest suits people who want a filter pitcher, a shower filter or an under-sink system from a US company, and homeowners who already know what is in their water and want a system matched to it. It's a poor fit if you want to try a filter and send it back freely, or if you aren't sure which system you need yet.
